coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 3
record.summary: Planned office/laboratory block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a flat 130 ft height limit; residential uses are not permitted here; no design review approval or construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. West edge corrected 2026-09-16 (fifth pass) against Maryland Street's real, directly-measured near curb, cross-validated against the source diagram's own printed scale (which independently implies a similar block width) -- treat that edge as accurate to roughly 5-10m. The north, south, and east edges still carry the original 10-25m diagram-transform tolerance and have not been independently re-verified against satellite imagery. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 130 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3. The D4D's own Permitted Uses table marks residential NOT PERMITTED on this block, while Laboratory and Life Science uses ARE permitted -- i.e., this is planned as an office/lab block, not residential, contrary to a sometimes-cited secondhand description. It does not front the Louisiana Paseo (a separate, physically distant open space between Blocks 15 and 7). No construction-start source found.

facts.value: Non-Retail Sales/Services (office) and Laboratory/Life Science uses permitted; Residential Not Permitted (D4D final Table 3.1.1)
flat 130 ft max per the D4D's Figure 6.2.3

One or more of Blocks 2, 3, 11, 12 or 15 must be deed-restricted for Life Science/Laboratory uses under the Development Agreement's Phasing Plan (as adopted; a July 2022 Planning Commission resolution separately removed an earlier, block-specific 130,000 sq ft life-science requirement tied to Block 15 -- see that record)
Not listed among the six Phase 1 blocks (2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15) named in the 2024 annual compliance report

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement that first names Block 3 as a development block under the adopted Design for Development's Land Use Table; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 3; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.
No phase-specific schedule found for Block 3; the added expected-completion milestone therefore uses only the whole-project buildout target (2035, SocketSite Oct 2020), not a block-specific date.
